subproblems.title: Retraction onto the n-skeleton away from the dual skeleton (Simon 6.5.4)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m + 1 < P and put n := m + 1. There is a constant c > 0, depending only on P and m, such that for every a ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P) with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 for all i the following holds. Let L*(a) := {y ∈ ℝ^P : there is a finite set s of coordinate indices with |s| ≥ m + 2 and y_i − a_i ∈ ℤ for all i ∈ s} (the dual skeleton) and d(x) := dist(x, L*(a)) (Metric.infDist). Then there is a map ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P such that (i) for every x with d(x) > 0, ψ(x) lies in the n-skeleton of the unit cubical grid, i.e. there is a set s of coordinate indices with P ≤ n + |s| and ψ(x)_i ∈ ℤ for all i ∈ s, and |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P; (ii) for every r with 0 < r ≤ 1/4 and all x, y with d(x) ≥ r and d(y) ≥ r, |ψ(x) − ψ(y)| ≤ (c/r)|x − y|.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 5.4 (chapter-06.txt, proof of 5.4 inside lines 1405–1928), as written out in Part D of the parent proof. It applies the documented correction |y − a| ≥ 1/4 (Simon prints 3/4) and states the cone property with the periodically translated planes split off.

Notation. n := m + 1, ℓ := P − n ≥ 1. For J ⊆ {1,…,P} with |J| = j and b ∈ ℤ^P, the closed j-face is F = F(b, J) := {x : b_i ≤ x_i ≤ b_i + 1 (i ∈ J), x_i = b_i (i ∉ J)}. J are its free coordinates, aff F := {x : x_i = b_i (i ∉ J)}, F̆ is its relative interior and ∂F := F ∖ F̆ is the union of its (j − 1)-faces. L_j := union of all closed j-faces. A point x lies in L_j iff at least P − j of its coordinates are integers: a point of F(b, J) has the P − j integer coordinates x_i = b_i (i ∉ J); conversely, if x_i ∈ ℤ for i in a set of P − j indices, let J be the complementary j indices and put b_i := ⌊x_i⌋ (i ∈ J), b_i := x_i (i ∉ J). In particular a point of L_n satisfies the statement's condition “∃ s, P ≤ n + |s|, x_i ∈ ℤ (i ∈ s)”. C := [0,1]^P. The coordinates of a satisfy a_i ∈ (1/4, 3/4). L*(a) is the set of y with at least n + 1 coordinates in a_i + ℤ, and d(x) := dist(x, L*(a)). d is 1-Lipschitz, and d(x) > 0 implies x ∉ L*(a). For a map f and a point x of its domain, D̄f(x) := limsup_{y→x} |f(y) − f(x)|/|y − x| (pointwise upper Lipschitz constant, y in the domain).

1. Centres of faces. For a face F = F(b, J) with |J| = j ≥ n + 1 put a_F ∈ aff F, (a_F)_i := b_i + a_i (i ∈ J), (a_F)_i := b_i (i ∉ J). Since a_i ∈ (1/4, 3/4), a_F ∈ F̆ and every point of ∂F (some free coordinate equal to b_i or b_i + 1) has distance > 1/4 from a_F. F − a_F contains the ball of radius 1/4 of the plane V_J := span{e_i : i ∈ J} and is contained in the ball of radius √j. A face shared by two cubes gets the same centre, because a_F is defined from F alone.

2. The dual skeleton meets a face in a cone. Let F = F(b, J), |J| = j ≥ n + 1. Then L*(a) ∩ F = U_F ∩ F, where U_F := ⋃ {Π_{J'} : J' ⊆ J, |J'| = n + 1} and Π_{J'} := {x ∈ aff F : x_i = (a_F)_i (i ∈ J')}. Proof: if x ∈ F ∩ L*(a), take s with |s| ≥ n + 1 and x_i − a_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s. For i ∉ J, x_i = b_i ∈ ℤ while a_i ∉ ℤ, so s ⊆ J. For i ∈ s, x_i − b_i ∈ [0, 1] and x_i − b_i ≡ a_i (mod 1) with a_i ∈ (1/4, 3/4), so x_i = b_i + a_i = (a_F)_i; any J' ⊆ s with |J'| = n + 1 gives x ∈ Π_{J'}. Conversely, if x ∈ F ∩ Π_{J'} then x_i − a_i = b_i ∈ ℤ for the n + 1 indices i ∈ J', so x ∈ L*(a). Each Π_{J'} is an affine subspace of aff F through a_F. So U_F is invariant under every homothety of aff F centred at a_F with nonzero ratio, and a_F ∈ L*(a).

3. Radial retractions. For F as in 2, let N_F be the gauge of the convex body F − a_F in V_J (N_F(v) = max_{i∈J} max(v_i/(1 − a_i), −v_i/a_i)), and put ψ_F(x) := a_F + (x − a_F)/N_F(x − a_F) for x ∈ F ∖ {a_F}. ψ_F(x) is the point of ∂F on the ray from a_F through x, and ψ_F = id on ∂F. By 1, N_F is 4-Lipschitz and N_F(v) ≥ |v|/√j. If x ∈ F ∖ L*(a) then x ∉ U_F, hence ψ_F(x) = a_F + λ(x − a_F) (λ > 0) ∉ U_F by the homothety invariance of U_F, hence ψ_F(x) ∈ ∂F ∖ L*(a) by 2. If x lies in two j-faces F ≠ F', then x lies in their intersection, a face of dimension < j, so x ∈ ∂F ∩ ∂F' and ψ_F(x) = x = ψ_{F'}(x). Hence ψ^{(j)} := ⋃_{|J|=j} ψ_F is a well-defined map L_j ∖ L*(a) → L_{j−1} ∖ L*(a). It is continuous because the j-faces form a locally finite closed cover of L_j and each ψ_F is continuous on F ∖ {a_F}. Radial estimate: for x, y ∈ F ∖ {a_F}, with v := x − a_F, w := y − a_F,
 |ψ_F(x) − ψ_F(y)| = |v/N_F(v) − w/N_F(w)| ≤ |v − w|/N_F(v) + |w| |N_F(w) − N_F(v)|/(N_F(v)N_F(w)) ≤ (1 + 4√j)√j |v − w|/|v|,
so D̄(ψ_F|F)(x) ≤ (1 + 4√j)√j/|x − a_F|.

4. Definition of ψ. On ℝ^P ∖ L*(a) put ψ := ψ^{(n+1)} ∘ ψ^{(n+2)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^{(P)} (L_P = ℝ^P). By 3 it is well defined and continuous, and it takes values in L_n ∖ L*(a). On L*(a) put ψ := id (never used). This proves the first half of (i) for every x with d(x) > 0. Same cube: if x ∈ z + C (z ∈ ℤ^P) and x ∉ L*(a), then ψ^{(P)}(x) = ψ_{z+C}(x) ∈ z + C. Inductively, if y ∈ (z + C) ∩ L_j ∖ L*(a), then y lies in a j-face G ⊆ z + C (its integer coordinates are z_i or z_i + 1; fix those), and ψ^{(j)}(y) = ψ_G(y) ∈ ∂G ⊆ z + C (any j-face containing y gives the same value by 3). Hence ψ(x) ∈ z + C and |ψ(x) − x| ≤ diam(z + C) = √P, which is the second half of (i). Also ψ(z + x) = z + ψ(x) for z ∈ ℤ^P, since L*(a) + z = L*(a) and the faces, centres and retractions are translated accordingly.

5. Pointwise bound D̄ψ(x) ≤ c₁(P, n)/d(x) for every x with d(x) > 0. The proof is by induction on ℓ = P − n ≥ 1, simultaneously for all P, n with that codimension and all admissible a. Points y near x lie in one of the finitely many closed unit cubes containing x, and the bound is proved on each of them; by periodicity we may take the cube to be C.
 (5a) ℓ = 1, i.e. P = n + 1. By 2 with F = C (j = P = n + 1, only J' = J), L*(a) ∩ C = {a}, and ψ = ψ^{(P)} = ψ_C on C. By 3, D̄(ψ|C)(x) ≤ (1 + 4√P)√P/|x − a| ≤ (1 + 4√P)√P/d(x), because a ∈ L*(a). So c₁(n + 1, n) := (1 + 4√(n+1))√(n+1).
 (5b) ℓ ≥ 2. On C ∖ L*(a), ψ = ψ̃ ∘ ψ_C, with ψ_C = ψ^{(P)} and ψ̃ := ψ^{(n+1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^{(P−1)} on ∂C ∖ L*(a). Let y₀ := ψ_C(x) ∈ ∂C and let F be any (P − 1)-face of C containing y₀; for y ∈ C near x, ψ_C(y) is near y₀ and lies in one of the finitely many (P − 1)-faces of C containing y₀. Fix such an F = F(b, J), J = {1,…,P} ∖ {i₀}, b_{i₀} ∈ {0, 1}, b_i = 0 (i ∈ J). Identify aff F with ℝ^{P−1} by deleting the coordinate i₀. Under this identification:
 - the grid faces lying in aff F are the grid faces of ℝ^{P−1};
 - the centre of a face G ⊆ aff F is the centre of G for a' := (a_i)_{i ≠ i₀} (coordinates in (1/4, 3/4));
 - L := L*(a) ∩ aff F is the dual skeleton of ℝ^{P−1} for a' and the same n (the coordinate b_{i₀} ∈ ℤ is never in a_{i₀} + ℤ);
 - ψ̃ restricted to aff F ∖ L is the map of this construction for (P − 1, n, a'), whose codimension is ℓ − 1 ≥ 1. Indeed, a point y ∈ aff F ∩ L_j has at least (P − 1) − j integer coordinates besides y_{i₀}, so it lies in a j-face G ⊆ aff F, and by the consistency in 3 the value ψ^{(j)}(y) may be computed with such a G.
 By the induction hypothesis, D̄(ψ̃|F)(y₀) ≤ c₁(P − 1, n)/dist(y₀, L).
 Distance estimate. L is the union, over J' ⊆ J with |J'| = n + 1 and integers z_i (i ∈ J'), of the planes {u ∈ aff F : u_i = a_i + z_i (i ∈ J')}. Let L₀ be the union of those with all z_i = 0 and L₁ the union of the others. If some z_i ≠ 0 then a_i + z_i lies at distance > 1/4 from [0, 1], so dist(y₀, L₁) ≥ 1/4 for y₀ ∈ F. Let K₀ := ⋃_{J'} {u ∈ ℝ^P : u_i = a_i (i ∈ J')} (J' ⊆ J, |J'| = n + 1). Then K₀ ⊆ L*(a); K₀ is a union of affine subspaces through a, hence invariant under homotheties centred at a; and for u ∈ aff F, dist(u, K₀) = dist(u, L₀) (the coordinate i₀ is unconstrained in each plane of K₀). Since x ∈ C, y₀ = a + λ(x − a) with λ := 1/N_C(x − a) ≥ 1. Therefore dist(y₀, L₀) = dist(y₀, K₀) = λ dist(x, K₀) ≥ λ d(x). As d(x) ≤ |x − a|, λ d(x) ≤ |y₀ − a| ≤ √P, so dist(y₀, L) ≥ min(λ d(x), 1/4) ≥ λ d(x)/(4√P).
 Chain rule. Choose δ > 0 such that every (P − 1)-face of C meeting B_δ(y₀) contains y₀ (the finitely many faces not containing y₀ are at positive distance), and such that the induction bound holds up to ε on B_δ(y₀) for each of the finitely many faces containing y₀. By continuity of ψ_C, ψ_C(y) ∈ B_δ(y₀) for y ∈ C close to x. For such y, with F_y a (P − 1)-face containing ψ_C(y) and y₀,
 |ψ(y) − ψ(x)| ≤ (D̄(ψ̃|F_y)(y₀) + ε)|ψ_C(y) − y₀| ≤ (max_F D̄(ψ̃|F)(y₀) + ε)(D̄(ψ_C|C)(x) + ε)|y − x|.
 Using 3 for ψ_C and |y₀ − a| > 1/4,
 D̄(ψ|C)(x) ≤ 4√P c₁(P − 1, n)/(λ d(x)) · (1 + 4√P)√P/|x − a| = 4P(1 + 4√P)c₁(P − 1, n)/(|y₀ − a| d(x)) ≤ 16P(1 + 4√P)c₁(P − 1, n)/d(x).
 So c₁(P, n) := 16P(1 + 4√P)c₁(P − 1, n) works; it depends only on P and n. Taking the maximum over the finitely many closed cubes containing x (each handled by translation, with its own centre a + z ∈ L*(a)) gives D̄ψ(x) ≤ c₁/d(x), c₁ := c₁(P, n).

6. Lipschitz bound on {d ≥ r}. Let 0 < r ≤ 1/4 and d(x), d(y) ≥ r.
 (6a) Case |x − y| < r/2. Every point w of the segment [x, y] satisfies d(w) ≥ d(x) − |w − x| > r/2, so D̄ψ(w) < 2c₁/r by 5. The function f(t) := ψ(x + t(y − x)) is continuous on [0, 1] with limsup_{s→t}|f(s) − f(t)|/|s − t| ≤ (2c₁/r)|y − x| for every t. Then |f(1) − f(0)| ≤ (2c₁/r)|y − x|. To see this, for ε > 0 let t* := sup{t ∈ [0,1] : |f(s) − f(0)| ≤ ((2c₁/r)|y − x| + ε)s for all s ≤ t}. By continuity the inequality holds at t*; if t* < 1, the bound at t* extends it to [t*, t* + δ] for some δ > 0, a contradiction. Let ε ↓ 0.
 (6b) Case |x − y| ≥ r/2. By (i), |ψ(x) − ψ(y)| ≤ |ψ(x) − x| + |x − y| + |y − ψ(y)| ≤ 2√P + |x − y| ≤ (4√P/r)|x − y| + (1/(4r))|x − y|, using r ≤ 1/4.
 Hence (ii) holds with c := 2c₁ + 4√P + 1 > 0, which depends only on P and m. ∎
proof_key_steps: Faces F(b, J), centres a_F (free coordinates b_i + a_i), distance > 1/4 from a_F to ∂F.
L*(a) ∩ F is the union of affine planes of aff F through a_F (prescribed coordinates must be free and equal b_i + a_i), so it is a cone with vertex a_F.
Radial retractions ψ_F : F ∖ {a_F} → ∂F map F ∖ L*(a) into ∂F ∖ L*(a), agree on common faces, and satisfy D̄ψ_F ≤ (1 + 4√j)√j/|x − a_F|.
ψ := ψ^{(n+1)} ∘ ⋯ ∘ ψ^{(P)} maps {d > 0} into L_n, keeps each point in its closed unit cube (|ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P) and is ℤ^P-periodic.

Induction on ℓ = P − n: D̄ψ ≤ c₁/d, using the (P − 1)-face induction hypothesis, the split L = L₀ ∪ L₁ (periodic planes at distance ≥ 1/4), homogeneity of the cone K₀ ⊆ L*(a) about a, and |ψ_C(x) − a| ≥ 1/4 (corrected from Simon's 3/4).
Segment argument for |x − y| < r/2 and the bound 2√P + |x − y| otherwise give the Lipschitz constant (2c₁ + 4√P + 1)/r on {d ≥ r}.

subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m + 1 < P. There is C ∈ ℝ≥0, depending only on P and m, such that for any two finite Borel measures μ, μ' on ℝ^P there is a ∈ ℝ^P with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 for all i such that, writing L*(a) := {y : there is a finite set s of coordinate indices with |s| ≥ m + 2 and y_i − a_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s} and d := dist(·, L*(a)) (Metric.infDist), for every r with 0 < r ≤ 1/4: μ({x : d(x) < r}) ≤ C r^{m+2} μ(ℝ^P) and μ'({x : d(x) < r}) ≤ C r^{m+2} μ'(ℝ^P) (inequalities in [0, ∞], r^{m+2} read via ENNReal.ofReal).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (1)–(7) (chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928), as written out in step E1 of the parent proof, with μ_T and μ_{∂T} replaced by two arbitrary finite Borel measures μ, μ'.

Notation. n := m + 1, ℓ := P − n ≥ 1, so n + 1 ≤ P. 𝒥 := the set of J ⊆ {1,…,P} with |J| = n + 1, N := |𝒥| = binom(P, n + 1). For J ∈ 𝒥: S_J := {x : x_i = 0 (i ∉ J)} (dimension n + 1); p_J is the orthogonal projection onto S_J (p_J(x)_i = x_i for i ∈ J, 0 otherwise); S_J^⊥ = {x : x_i = 0 (i ∈ J)} (dimension ℓ − 1); Z_J := ℤ^P ∩ S_J; B^J_r(w) := {v ∈ S_J : |v − w| < r}. q := (1/2,…,1/2), x_J := p_J(q). L^d is Lebesgue measure, ω_d := L^d(unit ball of ℝ^d), ω_0 := 1. For a ∈ ℝ^P, L*(a) := {y : at least n + 1 = m + 2 coordinates satisfy y_i − a_i ∈ ℤ} and d_a := dist(·, L*(a)).

1. Tubes around the dual skeleton. For a ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0,
 {x : d_a(x) < r} = ⋃_{J∈𝒥} ⋃_{z∈Z_J} p_J^{-1}(B^J_r(p_J(a) + z)).
 Proof: L*(a) = ⋃_{J,z} A_{J,z} with A_{J,z} := p_J^{-1}(p_J(a) + z) = {y : y_i = a_i + z_i (i ∈ J)}. Indeed, if y ∈ L*(a), choose n + 1 indices J among those with y_i − a_i ∈ ℤ and put z_i := y_i − a_i (i ∈ J), z_i := 0 otherwise; the converse is immediate. For x ∈ ℝ^P, dist(x, A_{J,z}) = |p_J(x) − p_J(a) − z| (Pythagoras; the point x − p_J(x) + p_J(a) + z ∈ A_{J,z} attains it). The distance to a union is the infimum of the distances, so d_a(x) < r iff |p_J(x) − p_J(a) − z| < r for some (J, z).

2. Bad sets. Let ν be a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P and β > 0. For g ∈ S_J and r > 0 put O_r(g) := ⋃_{z∈Z_J} p_J^{-1}(B^J_r(g + z)) (open). Let G_J(ν) be the set of g ∈ S_J with |g − x_J| < 1/4 and ν(O_r(g)) ≤ β r^{n+1} ν(ℝ^P) for every r ∈ (0, 1/4], and B_J(ν) := {g ∈ S_J : |g − x_J| < 1/4} ∖ G_J(ν). If ν(ℝ^P) = 0 then B_J(ν) = ∅. Assume ν(ℝ^P) > 0.
 (2a) B_J(ν) is relatively open in S_J, hence Borel. Let g ∈ B_J(ν) with witness r and g_k → g in S_J. O_r(g_k) = O_r(g) + (g_k − g), and every point of the open set O_r(g) lies in O_r(g_k) for large k. So 1_{O_r(g)} ≤ liminf_k 1_{O_r(g_k)} pointwise and, by Fatou, ν(O_r(g)) ≤ liminf_k ν(O_r(g_k)). Hence ν(O_r(g_k)) > β r^{n+1} ν(ℝ^P) and |g_k − x_J| < 1/4 for large k, i.e. g_k ∈ B_J(ν).
 (2b) L^{n+1}(B_J(ν)) ≤ 5^{n+1} ω_{n+1}/β. For each b ∈ B_J(ν) choose r_b ∈ (0, 1/4] with ν(O_{r_b}(b)) > β r_b^{n+1} ν(ℝ^P). By the Vitali covering lemma (Simon Ch. 1, 3.4; Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement) there is a pairwise disjoint subfamily of the balls B^J_{r_b}(b), countable because S_J is separable, say B^J_{r_l}(b_l), such that every B^J_{r_b}(b) meets some B^J_{r_l}(b_l) with r_b ≤ 2r_l. So B_J(ν) ⊆ ⋃_l B^J_{5r_l}(b_l). The open sets O_{r_l}(b_l) are pairwise disjoint, because the balls B^J_{r_l}(b_l + z) are pairwise disjoint over (l, z): for equal z they are translates of disjoint balls; for z ≠ z' they lie in B^J_{1/2}(x_J + z) and B^J_{1/2}(x_J + z') (|b_l − x_J| < 1/4, r_l ≤ 1/4), which are disjoint as |z − z'| ≥ 1. Preimages under p_J of disjoint sets are disjoint. Hence β ν(ℝ^P) Σ_l r_l^{n+1} ≤ Σ_l ν(O_{r_l}(b_l)) ≤ ν(ℝ^P), so Σ_l r_l^{n+1} ≤ 1/β and L^{n+1}(B_J(ν)) ≤ Σ_l ω_{n+1}(5r_l)^{n+1} ≤ 5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}/β.

3. Choice of β and a. Put β := 1 + 2N·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ}·4^P/ω_P; it depends only on P and m. For J ∈ 𝒥 let Bad_J := {a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) : p_J(a) ∈ B_J(μ) ∪ B_J(μ')} (Borel). Write ℝ^P = S_J ⊕ S_J^⊥; the coordinate splitting x ↦ ((x_i)_{i∈J}, (x_i)_{i∉J}) is a measure-preserving equivalence of Lebesgue measure on Euclid P with the product of Lebesgue measures (Mathlib volume_preserving for coordinate permutations and products of PiLp/EuclideanSpace). Fubini gives
 L^P(Bad_J) = ∫_{B_J(μ)∪B_J(μ')} L^{ℓ−1}({w ∈ S_J^⊥ : g + w ∈ B_{1/4}(q)}) dL^{n+1}(g) ≤ (2·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}/β)·ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ},
because each fibre lies in a ball of radius 1/4 of the (ℓ − 1)-dimensional space S_J^⊥ (for ℓ = 1 the fibre has at most one point and L^0 is counting measure, ω_0 = 1). Summing over the N sets J, L^P(⋃_J Bad_J) ≤ 2N·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ}/β < ω_P 4^{−P} = L^P(B_{1/4}(q)). Choose a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) ∖ ⋃_J Bad_J. Then |a_i − 1/2| ≤ |a − q| < 1/4 for every i. For every J, |p_J(a) − x_J| ≤ |a − q| < 1/4 and p_J(a) ∉ B_J(μ) ∪ B_J(μ'), so p_J(a) ∈ G_J(μ) if μ(ℝ^P) > 0 and p_J(a) ∈ G_J(μ') if μ'(ℝ^P) > 0.

4. Conclusion. Let r ∈ (0, 1/4]. By 1, {x : d_a(x) < r} = ⋃_J O_r(p_J(a)), hence μ({d_a < r}) ≤ Σ_J μ(O_r(p_J(a))) ≤ N β r^{n+1} μ(ℝ^P); if μ(ℝ^P) = 0 both sides vanish. The same holds for μ'. Thus C := Nβ (as an element of ℝ≥0, depending only on P and m) satisfies μ({x : d_a(x) < r}) ≤ C r^{m+2} μ(univ) and μ'({x : d_a(x) < r}) ≤ C r^{m+2} μ'(univ) for all r ∈ (0, 1/4], with r^{m+2} = r^{n+1}. ∎
proof_key_steps: {d_a < r} is the union over (n+1)-subsets J and z ∈ ℤ^P ∩ S_J of the cylinders p_J^{-1}(B_r(p_J(a) + z)).

For each J and each measure, the set of bad projections g (some r ≤ 1/4 with ν(O_r(g)) > βr^{n+1}ν(ℝ^P)) is relatively open (Fatou) and has L^{n+1}-measure ≤ 5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}/β by the Vitali 5r-covering lemma and disjointness of the periodic cylinders.
Fubini over S_J × S_J^⊥ bounds the measure of centres a ∈ B_{1/4}(q) with a bad projection by 2·5^{n+1}ω_{n+1}ω_{ℓ−1}4^{1−ℓ}/β; for β large the union over J misses a point a.
For this a, μ({d_a < r}) ≤ Σ_J μ(O_r(p_J(a))) ≤ Nβ r^{n+1}μ(ℝ^P), likewise for μ'; C := Nβ.

subproblems.title: Poincaré and trace inequalities on the unit cube with an integer median
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} (Euclid n, Lebesgue measure), and div G := trace of the derivative (LinearMap.trace of fderiv). There is c > 0, depending only on m, such that: if u : ℝⁿ → ℝ is integer-valued (u(y) ∈ ℤ for every y), integrable on Q₁, and V ∈ ℝ satisfies ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y, then there is β ∈ ℤ with (1) ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ cV, (2) |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|, and (3) |∫_{Q₁}(u − β) · div G| ≤ cV for every C^∞ map G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with |G(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ m : ℕ, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (u : Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (V : ℝ), (∀ y, ∃ z : ℤ, u y = z) → IntegrableOn u {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ g : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, u y * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ g y) ≤ V) → ∃ β : ℤ, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y - β| ≤ c * V ∧ |(β : ℝ)| ≤ 2 * ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, |u y| ∧ ∀ G : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) G → (∀ y, ‖G y‖ ≤ 1) → |∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, (u y - β) * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ G y)| ≤ c * V
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Part C (C1, C2) of the parent proof, which replaces Simon's appeal to the BV facts Ch. 6, 2.35–2.37 and Ch. 2, 2.7, 2.9 in displays (26)–(33) of the proof of 5.1. Conclusion (3) is C1(ii) written without currents: the boundary mass of u[[Q₁]] tested on the field G that represents an (n − 1)-form.

Notation. n := m + 1 ≥ 1, Q₁ := (0,1)ⁿ ⊆ ℝⁿ (Lebesgue measure Lⁿ, Lⁿ(Q₁) = 1), div G := trace DG. For 0 < δ < 1/8, Q_δ := (δ, 1 − δ)ⁿ (side s = 1 − 2δ ∈ [3/4, 1]). φ ∈ C_c^∞(B_1(0)), φ ≥ 0, ∫φ = 1, φ_σ(z) := σ^{−n}φ(z/σ), φ̌_σ(z) := φ_σ(−z). ū := u·1_{Q₁} ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ), u_σ := ū ∗ φ_σ ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ). Let u, V be as in the statement.

0. Preliminaries. Taking g = 0 gives V ≥ 0. Applying the hypothesis to g and −g gives |∫_{Q₁} u div g| ≤ V for every admissible g (smooth, compact support in Q₁, |g| ≤ 1). For every constant β and admissible g, ∫_{Q₁} β div g = 0 (integrate each ∂_i g_i along lines; g has compact support in Q₁). Hence v := u − β is integrable on Q₁ and satisfies the same hypothesis with the same V.

1. Gradient bound: for 0 < σ < δ < 1/8, ∫_{Q_δ} |∇u_σ| ≤ V. For g ∈ C_c^∞(Q_δ; ℝⁿ) with |g| ≤ 1, Fubini and differentiation under the convolution give ∫ ∇u_σ · g = −∫ u_σ div g = −∫ ū (φ̌_σ ∗ div g) = −∫_{Q₁} u div(φ̌_σ ∗ g). Here φ̌_σ ∗ g is smooth with compact support in Q_δ + B_σ(0) ⊆ Q₁ and |φ̌_σ ∗ g| ≤ 1, so the right side is ≤ V by 0. The supremum of ∫ ∇u_σ · g over such g equals ∫_{Q_δ}|∇u_σ|: take g_k := χ_k ∇u_σ/(|∇u_σ|² + 1/k)^{1/2} with smooth cut-offs 0 ≤ χ_k ≤ 1, χ_k ↑ 1_{Q_δ}, and use monotone convergence. This proves the bound.

2. Smooth Poincaré inequality. For a cube Q' of side s ∈ [1/2, 1] and v ∈ C¹(closure Q'), ∫_{Q'} |v − v_{Q'}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n ∫_{Q'} |∇v|, where v_{Q'} is the mean. Indeed |v(x) − v(y)| ≤ √n s ∫_0^1 |∇v(x + t(y − x))| dt for x, y ∈ Q'. Integrate over Q' × Q'; for t ≤ 1/2 substitute x ↦ (1 − t)x + ty (Jacobian (1 − t)ⁿ ≥ 2^{−n}, image ⊆ Q' by convexity), and for t ≥ 1/2 substitute y ↦ (1 − t)x + ty (Jacobian tⁿ ≥ 2^{−n}). This gives ∫∫ |v(x) − v(y)| dx dy ≤ √n s · 2ⁿ sⁿ ∫_{Q'} |∇v|. Since |v(x) − v_{Q'}| ≤ s^{−n}∫_{Q'}|v(x) − v(y)| dy, ∫_{Q'} |v − v_{Q'}| ≤ √n s 2ⁿ ∫_{Q'}|∇v| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n ∫_{Q'}|∇v|.

3. Poincaré inequality for u: ∫_{Q₁} |u − u_{Q₁}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V. By 1 and 2 (Q' = Q_δ), ∫_{Q_δ}|u_σ − (u_σ)_{Q_δ}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V for σ < δ. As σ ↓ 0, u_σ → ū in L¹(ℝⁿ) (continuity of translation in L¹), so ∫_{Q_δ}|u − u_{Q_δ}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V. As δ ↓ 0, u_{Q_δ} → u_{Q₁} and ∫_{Q_δ}|u − u_{Q_δ}| → ∫_{Q₁}|u − u_{Q₁}| by dominated convergence.

4. Integer median (C2). Since u is real-valued and integrable, Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ c}) → 1 as c → +∞ and → 0 as c → −∞. Let β be the least integer c with Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ c}) ≥ 1/2. Then Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β}) ≥ 1/2 and, since u is integer-valued, Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≥ β}) = 1 − Lⁿ(Q₁ ∩ {u ≤ β − 1}) > 1/2.
 (a) β minimizes c ↦ ∫_{Q₁}|u − c|. For c > β, |u − c| − |u − β| ≥ c − β on {u ≤ β} and ≥ −(c − β) on {u > β}, so ∫(|u − c| − |u − β|) ≥ (c − β)(Lⁿ{u ≤ β} − Lⁿ{u > β}) ≥ 0. The case c < β is symmetric, using Lⁿ{u ≥ β} ≥ 1/2. With c = u_{Q₁} and 3: ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V.
 (b) If β > 0 then u ≥ β on a set of measure ≥ 1/2, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ β/2. If β < 0 then u ≤ β on a set of measure ≥ 1/2, so ∫_{Q₁}|u| ≥ |β|/2. Hence |β| ≤ 2∫_{Q₁}|u|.

5. Trace estimate. Let G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be smooth with |G| ≤ 1, and let w ∈ L¹(Q₁) satisfy the hypothesis of the statement with the constant V. Then |∫_{Q₁} w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q₁}|w|.
 Proof. Let w_σ := (w 1_{Q₁}) ∗ φ_σ, σ < δ. Apply the divergence theorem on the box Q_δ to the smooth field w_σG, whose divergence is ∇w_σ · G + w_σ div G. (By Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus in each coordinate, ∫_{Q_δ} ∂_i(w_σG_i) = ∫ over the two faces {x_i = 1 − δ}, {x_i = δ} of ±w_σG_i; alternatively use Mathlib MeasureTheory.integral_divergence_of_hasFDerivAt_off_countable, transported from Fin n → ℝ to Euclid n.) This gives ∫_{Q_δ} w_σ div G = −∫_{Q_δ} ∇w_σ · G + ∫_{∂Q_δ} w_σ G · ν dH^{n−1}, so |∫_{Q_δ} w_σ div G| ≤ ∫_{Q_δ}|∇w_σ| + ∫_{∂Q_δ}|w_σ|. On the face {x₁ = δ}, |w_σ(δ, x')| ≤ |w_σ(x₁, x')| + ∫_δ^{1−δ}|∂₁w_σ(t, x')| dt for x₁ ∈ (δ, 1 − δ). Averaging over x₁ (length s ≥ 1/2) and integrating in x' gives ∫_{face}|w_σ| ≤ 2∫_{Q_δ}|w_σ| + ∫_{Q_δ}|∇w_σ|; the same holds for all 2n faces. With 1 applied to w: |∫_{Q_δ} w_σ div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q_δ}|w_σ|. Let σ ↓ 0 (w_σ → w 1_{Q₁} in L¹, and div G is bounded on closure Q₁), then δ ↓ 0 (dominated convergence): |∫_{Q₁} w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫_{Q₁}|w|.

6. Conclusion. Put c := 2^{n+1}√n + (2n + 1) + 4n·2^{n+1}√n > 0 (depending only on m). By 4(a), ∫_{Q₁}|u − β| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V ≤ cV, which is (1); 4(b) is (2). By 0, w := u − β satisfies the hypothesis with V, so by 5 and 4(a), for every smooth G with |G| ≤ 1, |∫_{Q₁}(u − β) div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n·2^{n+1}√n V ≤ cV, which is (3). ∎
proof_key_steps: V ≥ 0, |∫u div g| ≤ V, and u − β satisfies the same hypothesis.
Mollified u_σ satisfies ∫_{Q_δ}|∇u_σ| ≤ V (duality with fields φ̌_σ ∗ g supported in Q₁).
Smooth Poincaré on cubes of side in [1/2, 1] and the limits σ ↓ 0, δ ↓ 0 give ∫_{Q₁}|u − u_{Q₁}| ≤ 2^{n+1}√n V.
The least integer β with Lⁿ{u ≤ β} ≥ 1/2 is a median (integer values), minimizes c ↦ ∫|u − c| and satisfies |β| ≤ 2∫|u|.
Divergence theorem and the elementary trace inequality on Q_δ give |∫_{Q₁} w div G| ≤ (2n + 1)V + 4n∫|w|; apply to w = u − β.

subproblems.title: Push-forward by dilations x ↦ λx (scaling of currents)
subproblems.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ there is an operation dil assigning to every degree k ∈ ℕ, real λ and current X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) (domain univ) a current dil_k(λ, X) ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) such that for every k and every λ > 0: (1) dil_k(λ, X − Y) = dil_k(λ, X) − dil_k(λ, Y) for all X, Y; (2) dil_k(λ⁻¹, dil_k(λ, X)) = X; (3) M(dil_k(λ, X)) = λ^k M(X) (in [0, ∞], factor ENNReal.ofReal (λ^k)); (4) spt dil_k(λ, X) = {λx : x ∈ spt X}; (5) dil_k(λ, X) is integer multiplicity whenever X is (every degree k, including 0); (6) ∂ dil_{k+1}(λ, X) = dil_k(λ, ∂X) for X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step E0 of the parent proof (scaling, Simon Ch. 6, 5.3 from 5.1). δ_{λ#} maps integer multiplicity currents to integer multiplicity currents (carrier δ_λ(M), same multiplicity and orientation; approximate tangent spaces commute with dilations), scales masses of k-currents by λ^k, commutes with ∂ and scales supports.

Notation. For λ ≠ 0, δ_λ(x) := λx. For a k-form ω on ℝ^P, (δ_λ^#ω)(x) := ω(λx) ∘ (λ·id), i.e. (δ_λ^#ω)(x)(v_1,…,v_k) = λ^k ω(λx)(v_1,…,v_k). |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|.

1. Definition. For λ ≠ 0 the affine map x ↦ 0 + (λ·id)x is a homeomorphism, hence proper. So SimonGMT's GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward (λ·id) 0 (Simon 6.2.23) defines, for X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) (domain univ, whose preimage is univ), a current dil_k(λ, X) := δ_{λ#}X with δ_{λ#}X(ω) = X(δ_λ^#ω). For λ = 0 put dil_k(0, X) := X (never used). Below λ > 0.

2. Linearity: dil(λ, X − Y)(ω) = (X − Y)(δ_λ^#ω) = X(δ_λ^#ω) − Y(δ_λ^#ω), so dil(λ, X − Y) = dil(λ, X) − dil(λ, Y) by GeometricCurrentOn.ext.

3. Inverse: δ_λ^#(δ_{λ⁻¹}^#ω)(x) = (δ_{λ⁻¹}^#ω)(λx)∘(λ·id) = ω(x)∘(λ⁻¹·id)∘(λ·id) = ω(x), so dil(λ⁻¹, dil(λ, X))(ω) = X(δ_λ^#δ_{λ⁻¹}^#ω) = X(ω).

4. Boundary: SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward (d commutes with affine pull-back, SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm) gives ∂ dil(λ, X) = dil(λ, ∂X) for X of degree k + 1.

5. Mass. For a k-covector α, (α∘(λ·id))(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_k}) = λ^k α(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_k}), hence |α∘(λ·id)| = λ^k|α| and |δ_λ^#ω(x)| = λ^k|ω(λx)|. If ω is admissible for M(dil(λ, X)) (test form, |ω| ≤ 1 everywhere), then η := δ_λ^#ω is a test form with |η| ≤ λ^k. So dil(λ, X)(ω) = X(η) ≤ λ^k M(X) (apply the definition of mass to λ^{−k}η, which is admissible; if M(X) = ∞ there is nothing to prove). Conversely, for η admissible for M(X), ω := λ^k δ_{λ⁻¹}^#η is admissible (|ω(y)| = λ^kλ^{−k}|η(y/λ)| ≤ 1) and δ_λ^#ω = λ^kη, so λ^k X(η) = dil(λ, X)(ω) ≤ M(dil(λ, X)). Taking suprema (in [0, ∞], with ENNReal.ofReal) gives M(dil(λ, X)) = λ^k M(X); for k = 0, λ^0 = 1.

6. Support. tsupport(δ_λ^#ω) = λ^{−1} tsupport ω. If W is open with compact closure, then so is λW. X vanishes on all test forms supported in W iff dil(λ, X) vanishes on all test forms supported in λW, because ω ↦ δ_λ^#ω is a bijection between test forms supported in λW and those supported in W, with inverse ω ↦ δ_{λ⁻¹}^#ω. Hence the zero region of dil(λ, X) is λ·(zero region of X), and spt dil(λ, X) = ℝ^P ∖ λ Z_X = λ(ℝ^P ∖ Z_X) = (x ↦ λx)(spt X).

7. Integer multiplicity. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep (domain univ, degree k) of X. Define M' := λM, θ'(y) := θ(y/λ), ξ'(y) := ξ(y/λ). Then:
 - M' is Borel (image of a Borel set under a homeomorphism) and countably k-rectifiable (compose the Lipschitz parametrizations with δ_λ; Hᵏ-null sets go to Hᵏ-null sets by the scaling below);
 - θ' is Borel, ℕ-valued and positive on M';
 - ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M' (composition with the homeomorphism δ_{λ⁻¹}, under which Hᵏ⌞M' and Hᵏ⌞M correspond up to the factor λ^k).
 Hausdorff scaling: Hᵏ(λA) = λ^k Hᵏ(A) for all A (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). So Hᵏ⌞(λM) = λ^k·(δ_λ)_*(Hᵏ⌞M) as measures (δ_λ is a measurable equivalence). By the change of variables for Bochner integrals under a measurable equivalence (Mathlib integral_map_equiv, integral_smul_measure), ∫_{λM} f dHᵏ = λ^k ∫_M f(λx) dHᵏ(x) for every f; both sides are 0 if one side is not integrable, since integrability is transported as well.
 Local integrability: for compact K, ∫_{M'∩K} θ' dHᵏ = λ^k∫_{M∩λ⁻¹K} θ dHᵏ < ∞.
 Approximate tangent spaces: with SimonGMT's blowUpMap x r (y) = r⁻¹(y − x), blowUpMap (λx) r '' (λM) = blowUpMap x (r/λ) '' M, and r ↦ r/λ maps the filter 𝓝[>] 0 onto itself. Therefore HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (λM) (λx) Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M x Q. Consequently, for Hᵏ-a.e. y ∈ M' (y = λx with x outside the exceptional null set of R), ξ'(y) = ξ(x) is a unit orientation of an approximate tangent space of M' at y. So R' := (M', θ', ξ') is an IMRep.
 It represents dil(λ, X). For every ω, ⟨(δ_λ^#ω)(x), ξ(x)⟩ = λ^k⟨ω(λx), ξ(x)⟩ (ξ(x) is a continuous linear functional on k-covectors, and δ_λ^#ω(x) = λ^k ω(λx) as k-covectors), so
 dil(λ, X)(ω) = X(δ_λ^#ω) = ∫_M θ(x) λ^k⟨ω(λx), ξ(x)⟩ dHᵏ(x) = ∫_{M'} θ'(y)⟨ω(y), ξ'(y)⟩ dHᵏ(y) = R'.action ω.
 This holds in every degree k, including k = 0.

8. The function dil : ∀ k, ℝ → 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) of 1 satisfies, for every k and λ > 0, the six properties of the statement by 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 4. ∎
proof_key_steps: dil_k(λ, X) := the SimonGMT affine push-forward along x ↦ λx (proper for λ ≠ 0), X(δ_λ^#ω).
Linearity, inverse (δ_λ^# δ_{λ⁻¹}^# = id) and boundary commutation (boundary_affinePushforward).
Coefficient norms scale by λ^k under δ_λ^#, giving M(dil(λ, X)) = λ^k M(X).
Zero regions scale by λ, giving spt dil(λ, X) = λ spt X.
The IMRep (λM, θ(·/λ), ξ(·/λ)) represents dil(λ, X): Hausdorff measure scales by λ^k and approximate tangent spaces are dilation invariant (blowUpMap (λx) r ∘ δ_λ = blowUpMap x (r/λ)).

(These are exactly the frozen Lean types of the parent node's resolved dependencies, written as antecedents so that the child does not need those declarations; the parent instantiates them.) Then there is S ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) such that: for every test form ω, the series Σ_i W_i(ω) has sum S(ω) (HasSum); M(S) ≤ Σ_i M(W_i); spt S ⊆ closure(⋃_i spt W_i); and if every W_i is integer multiplicity then S is integer multiplicity.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the closing step of B3 in the parent proof, together with the elementary fact that mass-summable series of currents define currents. That step combines countably many integer multiplicity pieces whose multiplicities have finite total integral into one integer multiplicity current, using the locality of approximate tangent spaces and the sign rule (L3). This replaces Simon's completeness theorem 3.13 in the parent proof (departure (i)).

Notation. All currents are in 𝒟_{n'}(ℝ^P) with domain univ, n' := k + 1. ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| (Euclidean coefficient norm). Hypotheses (VO), (MR), (IMC) are the three displayed hypotheses of the statement (frozen types of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub).

1. Evaluation bound. For every current X and test form ω, |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖ (in [0, ∞]). Indeed, if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0; otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ are admissible for M(X) (support in univ, |·| ≤ 1), so ±X(ω)/‖ω‖ ≤ M(X).

2. Definition of S. Let Σ_i M(W_i) =: A < ∞. For each ω, Σ_i |W_i(ω)| ≤ A‖ω‖ < ∞, so S(ω) := Σ_i W_i(ω) converges absolutely; in particular HasSum (i ↦ W_i(ω)) (S(ω)). S is linear. Continuity: if ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology (supports in one compact set, all derivatives → 0 uniformly), then sup_x of the operator norm of ω_j(x) tends to 0. The Euclidean coefficient norm is bounded by a constant C(P, n') times the operator norm (each coefficient ω(x)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_{n'}}) is bounded by the operator norm). Hence ‖ω_j‖ → 0 and |S(ω_j)| ≤ A‖ω_j‖ → 0. So S ∈ 𝒟_{n'}(ℝ^P).

3. Mass. For admissible ω, S(ω) = Σ_i W_i(ω) ≤ Σ_i M(W_i), so M(S) ≤ Σ_i M(W_i).

4. Support. Let E := closure ⋃_i spt W_i and x ∉ E. Choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ∩ E = ∅. The open ball B := ball(x, r) has compact closure. Every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B satisfies tsupport ω ∩ spt W_i = ∅ for all i, hence W_i(ω) = 0 by (VO) and S(ω) = 0. So x lies in the zero region of S, i.e. spt S ⊆ E.

5. Integer multiplicity. Assume every W_i is integer multiplicity, with IMRep R_i = (M_i, θ_i, ξ_i). By (MR) (U = W = univ, open), ∫_{M_i} θ_i dH^{n'} = R_i.measure(ℝ^P) = M(W_i). Modifying ξ_i on an H^{n'}⌞M_i-null set, we may take ξ_i Borel (this changes neither the action nor the a.e. orientation property).
 (5a) N := ⋃_i M_i is Borel and countably n'-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion), and H^{n'}(N) ≤ Σ_i H^{n'}(M_i) ≤ Σ_i ∫_{M_i}θ_i dH^{n'} = A < ∞ because θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i.
 (5b) Θ := Σ_i θ_i 1_{M_i} : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] has ∫ Θ dH^{n'} = A, so Θ < ∞ off an H^{n'}-null set. At such points only finitely many i have x ∈ M_i (θ_i ≥ 1 there).
 (5c) Tangent planes. For each i, apply (IMC)(a) with U = univ, M = M_i ⊆ M' = N (H^{n'}(N ∩ K) ≤ A < ∞): for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ M_i and every subspace Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n' M_i x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n' N x Q. By the orientation field of R_i, for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ M_i there is Q_i(x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n' M_i x Q_i(x) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_i(x)) (Q_i(x)). Removing a countable union of null sets, for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ N each i with x ∈ M_i gives an approximate tangent space Q_i(x) of N at x. By uniqueness (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) these coincide; call the common value Q(x).
 (5d) Signs. Let ι(x) := min{i : x ∈ M_i} for x ∈ N (Borel) and η(x) := ξ_{ι(x)}(x) (Borel). (L3) Two unit orientations of the same n'-dimensional subspace differ by a sign: if ξ = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) and ξ' = ±(α ↦ α(τ')) with orthonormal bases τ, τ' of Q, then τ' = Oτ for an orthogonal O, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Put s_i(x) := 1 if ‖ξ_i(x) − η(x)‖ ≤ ‖ξ_i(x) + η(x)‖ and s_i(x) := −1 otherwise (Borel). A unit orientation is nonzero (it takes the value ±1 on a covector dual to its orthonormal frame). So for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ N and every i with x ∈ M_i, ξ_i(x) = s_i(x)η(x).
 (5e) Multiplicity. m(x) := Σ_i s_i(x)θ_i(x)1_{M_i}(x) (set m := 0 where Θ(x) = ∞) is Borel, as a pointwise limit of finite sums of Borel integer-valued functions. H^{n'}-a.e. on N it is a finite sum of integers, and |m| ≤ Θ, so m is integer-valued a.e. with ∫|m| dH^{n'} ≤ A.
 (5f) Action. For a test form ω, |ξ_i(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ ‖ω‖ for a.e. x ∈ M_i ((IMC)(d)), so Σ_i ∫ θ_i 1_{M_i}|ξ_i(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖A. Dominated convergence for series gives
 S(ω) = Σ_i ∫_{M_i} θ_i ξ_i(x)(ω(x)) dH^{n'} = ∫_N Σ_i θ_i 1_{M_i} s_i η(x)(ω(x)) dH^{n'} = ∫_N m(x) η(x)(ω(x)) dH^{n'}.
 (5g) The IMRep. Let Z ⊆ N be a Borel H^{n'}-null set outside of which (5b)–(5e) hold. Put N' := {x ∈ N ∖ Z : m(x) ≠ 0} (Borel), mult := |m| on N' and 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued, positive on N'), and orient := sign(m)η. Check the IMRep fields:
 - N' ⊆ univ;
 - N' ⊆ N is countably n'-rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono);
 - local integrability: ∫_{N'∩K}|m| ≤ A < ∞;
 - orient is Borel;
 - for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ N', (IMC)(a) with M = N' ⊆ M' = N gives that Q(x), an approximate tangent space of N at x, is also one of N' at x, and sign(m(x))η(x) is a unit orientation of Q(x) (the definition IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign).
 Its action is ∫_{N'} |m| sign(m) η(ω) dH^{n'} = ∫_N m η(ω) dH^{n'} = S(ω) (m = 0 on N ∖ (N' ∪ Z)). Hence S is integer multiplicity.

6. The current S of 2 satisfies the four conclusions by 2, 3, 4 and 5. ∎
proof_key_steps: |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖, so S(ω) := Σ_i W_i(ω) converges absolutely and defines a sequentially continuous linear functional.
M(S) ≤ Σ M(W_i) by evaluating on admissible forms; spt S ⊆ closure ⋃ spt W_i by (VO).
For integer multiplicity W_i with IMReps (M_i, θ_i, ξ_i): N := ⋃M_i has finite Hausdorff measure by (MR), and a.e. point lies in finitely many M_i.
By (IMC)(a) and uniqueness all M_i containing x share the approximate tangent space of N at x; the orientations differ from a Borel reference orientation η by signs (sign rule).
The integer multiplicity m := Σ s_iθ_i1_{M_i} and dominated convergence give S(ω) = ∫_N mη(ω)dH, and (N', |m|, sign(m)η) is an IMRep of S.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Parts A and B of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.17–2.29 and 3.3–3.9: the homotopy formula and mass estimate 2.25–2.27, the Lipschitz push-forward 2.29, the integrality of push-forwards 3.3–3.9), packaged as two operators. Departure (i) of the parent (no appeal to Simon's completeness theorem 3.13) is kept: integrality comes from the integral representation B3, whose final combination step is the sibling cmcdt_im_series (IMS). The following departures from the parent text are all for the operator packaging needed by the sibling cmcdt_skeleton_deformation:
 - the cut-off in A4(f), which removes the parent's assumption that G − F be bounded;
 - B3 is used only for globally Lipschitz F; the parent's open set O and locally Lipschitz ψ are not needed, because the skeleton child sums integer multiplicity shell contributions with IMS instead of using Φ_ψ(T). So B1's refinement clause and the parametrization-independence remark of B4 are omitted;
 - Part C, which defines the two operators.

Conventions. (VO), (MR), (REP), (IMC) denote the four displayed hypotheses of the statement (frozen types of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub). IMS is the sibling theorem cmcdt_im_series, applied to (VO), (MR), (IMC). Currents are on univ in some ℝ^N = Euclid N; 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) are k-currents and 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) test k-forms. |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|, and for a k-vector ζ (a continuous linear functional on k-covectors) |ζ| := sup{ζ(α) : |α| ≤ 1}. NC_k(ℝ^N) is the set of X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with compact support, M(X) < ∞ and, if k ≥ 1, M(∂X) < ∞ (this is the statement's hypothesis IsCompact X.support, X.mass < ∞, boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞). NC is closed under differences: spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y and M(X − Y) ≤ M(X) + M(Y) (directly from the definitions). |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖ for every current (scale ω to be admissible). The zero current is integer multiplicity (empty carrier).

1. Multilinear algebra (parent (L0)–(L3)).
(L0) For a k-covector β, k!|β|² = Σ_{i_1,…,i_k} β(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_k})² =: ‖β‖²_HS (each increasing tuple occurs k! times up to sign, and tuples with repeats vanish). ‖·‖_HS is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the multilinear form, hence invariant under orthogonal changes of basis, and so are |·| and the dual norm on k-vectors.
(L1) For linear A : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} and a k-covector β on ℝ^{N'}, |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k|β|; dually |Λ_kAζ| ≤ ‖A‖^k|ζ|, where ⟨β, Λ_kAζ⟩ := ⟨A^#β, ζ⟩. By (L0) it suffices to bound ‖·‖_HS. Replacing one slot of a multilinear form γ by A multiplies its HS norm by at most ‖A‖ (for fixed other arguments, Σ_i γ(Ae_i, …)² = |Aᵀg|² ≤ ‖A‖²|g|², g the vector representing γ(·, …)); do this k times.
(L2) For a 1-covector β' and a k-covector γ, |β' ∧ γ| ≤ |β'||γ| (rotate so that β' = |β'|e¹ and use (L0)). Dually |v ∧ ζ| ≤ |v||ζ| for a vector v and a k-vector ζ, where ⟨β, v ∧ ζ⟩ := ⟨ι_vβ, ζ⟩, and |ι_vβ| ≤ |v||β|.
(L3) If τ_1,…,τ_k are orthonormal then ζ := τ_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_k (⟨α, ζ⟩ := α(τ_1,…,τ_k)) has |ζ| = 1. If A : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N is linear and injective, A = OS (S := (AᵀA)^{1/2}, O := AS^{−1} an isometric embedding). So Λ_kA(e_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ e_k) = det(S)·Oe_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ Oe_k, |Λ_kA(e)| = √det(AᵀA) =: JA, and Λ_kA(e)/JA is a unit simple k-vector orienting A(ℝᵏ). If A is not injective, Λ_kA(e) = 0 = JA. Two unit simple k-vectors orienting the same k-plane differ by a sign (the change of orthonormal basis has determinant ±1). By (IMC)(d), the orientation ξ of an IMRep satisfies |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.

Part A. Normal currents with compact support.

2. A0 (Representation). Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) have compact support and M(X) < ∞. (REP) with U = univ gives a Borel measure μ_X and ξ_X with μ_X(W) = M_W(X) for open W, |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ_X(ω) dμ_X. Then μ_X(ℝ^N) = M(X) < ∞. Moreover μ_X(ℝ^N ∖ spt X) = M_{ℝ^N∖spt X}(X) = 0, because every admissible ω supported in the open set ℝ^N ∖ spt X has X(ω) = 0 by (VO). Hence |X(ω)| ≤ ∫ |ω| dμ_X, and X(ω) = 0 whenever ω vanishes on spt X.

3. A1 (Smooth push-forward). Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) have compact support and F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be C^∞. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) put (F^#ω)(x) := ω(F(x)) ∘ DF(x) (Lean: (ω (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x)), a smooth k-form. Put F_#X(ω) := X(ζF^#ω) for ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^N) equal to 1 on a neighbourhood of spt X; this does not depend on ζ (two choices differ by a form vanishing near spt X; (VO)).
 - F_#X is a current: if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}) then ζF^#ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) by the chain and Leibniz rules (all derivatives of F are bounded on spt ζ).
 - ∂F_#X = F_#∂X: d commutes with F^# (SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin with U = V = univ), so ∂F_#X(ω) = X(ζ d(F^#ω)) = X(d(ζF^#ω)) − X(dζ ∧ F^#ω). The last term vanishes by (VO) since dζ = 0 near spt X, and X(d(ζF^#ω)) = ∂X(ζF^#ω) = F_#∂X(ω) (ζ = 1 near spt ∂X ⊆ spt X).
 - spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X): if tsupport ω ∩ F(spt X) = ∅, then F^#ω vanishes on the open set F^{-1}(ℝ^{N'} ∖ tsupport ω) ⊇ spt X, so tsupport(ζF^#ω) ∩ spt X = ∅ and F_#X(ω) = 0 by (VO). F(spt X) is compact, and a current vanishing on all forms supported in the complement of a closed set E has support in E (each point outside E has a ball with compact closure disjoint from E).
 - If M(X) < ∞, A0 gives F_#X(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω(F(x)), Λ_kDF(x)ξ_X(x)⟩ dμ_X(x). Hence by (L1), |F_#X(ω)| ≤ ∫ ‖DF‖^k|ω∘F| dμ_X and M(F_#X) ≤ sup_{spt X}‖DF‖^k M(X).

4. A2 (Product with [[0,1]]). We work directly in ℝ^{N+1} = Euclid (N + 1), writing its points as (t, x) with t the coordinate of index 0 and x ∈ ℝ^N the remaining ones (so no transport of currents is needed); e₀ := ∂_t. For a (k+1)-form ω on ℝ × ℝ^N let ω₁(t,x)(v_1,…,v_k) := ω(t,x)(e₀, (0,v_1),…,(0,v_k)) and ω₀ := ω − dt ∧ ω₁ (dt-free). For X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with compact support put ([[0,1]] × X)(ω) := X(∫_0^1 ω₁(t,·) dt) and ({s} × X)(ω) := X(i_s^#ω), i_s(x) := (s, x). The integrand is a smooth k-form with compact support (the projection of tsupport ω), and both are currents, with support in [0,1] × spt X and {s} × spt X respectively. Writing ω = dt ∧ ω₁ + ω₀, one has d(dt ∧ ω₁) = −dt ∧ d_xω₁ and dω₀ = dt ∧ ∂_tω₀ + d_xω₀, so (dω)₁ = ∂_tω₀ − d_xω₁. Integrating in t and using that d_x commutes with ∫dt,
 ∂([[0,1]] × X) = {1} × X − {0} × X − [[0,1]] × ∂X (k ≥ 1; for k = 0 the last term is absent).
If M(X) < ∞, A0 gives ([[0,1]] × X)(ω) = ∫_0^1∫ ⟨ω(t,x), e₀ ∧ ξ_X(x)⟩ dμ_X dt, so by (L2) M([[0,1]] × X) ≤ M(X); likewise M({s} × X) ≤ M(X). Hence for X ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N), [[0,1]] × X ∈ NC_{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with M(∂([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ 2M(X) + M(∂X).

5. A3 (Smooth homotopy formula). Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) have compact support, and let H : ℝ × ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be C^∞ with H(t, x) = F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) for (t, x) in a neighbourhood of [0,1] × spt X, F, G smooth. Since ∂H_# = H_#∂ (A1 in ℝ^{N+1}) and H_#({s} × X) = (H ∘ i_s)_#X with H ∘ i_1 = G, H ∘ i_0 = F near spt X, A2 gives
 G_#X − F_#X = ∂H_#([[0,1]] × X) + H_#([[0,1]] × ∂X) (last term absent for k = 0).
If M(X) < ∞: near [0,1] × spt X, DH(t,x)e₀ = (G − F)(x) and DH(t,x)(0,v) = ((1 − t)DF(x) + tDG(x))v. So Λ_{k+1}DH(e₀ ∧ ζ) = (G − F)(x) ∧ Λ_k((1 − t)DF + tDG)(x)ζ, and by A1, (L1), (L2)
 M(H_#([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ ∫ |G − F|(‖DF‖ + ‖DG‖)^k dμ_X ≤ sup_{spt X}|G − F| · sup_{spt X}(‖DF‖ + ‖DG‖)^k · M(X).

6. A4 (Lipschitz push-forward). Let X ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N) and let F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be Lipschitz with constant Λ. F_σ := F ∗ φ_σ (componentwise mollification, φ_σ a standard mollifier) is C^∞ with Lip F_σ ≤ Λ (so ‖DF_σ‖ ≤ Λ) and |F_σ − F| ≤ Λσ. Fix s ∈ C^∞(ℝ) with s(t) = t on [−1, 2] and s constant outside [−2, 3], so that s and s' are bounded. Apply A3 to F_σ, F_τ (H := F_σ + s(t)(F_τ − F_σ), smooth and globally Lipschitz because F_τ − F_σ is bounded by Λ(σ + τ)):
 |(F_σ)_#X(ω) − (F_τ)_#X(ω)| ≤ sup|F_σ − F_τ|((2Λ)^k M(X)‖dω‖ + (2Λ)^{k−1}M(∂X)‖ω‖) → 0 (σ, τ ↓ 0).
So F_#X(ω) := lim_{σ↓0}(F_σ)_#X(ω) exists. Properties:
 (a) |F_#X(ω)| ≤ Λ^k M(X)‖ω‖ (A1 for F_σ). So F_#X is linear and sequentially continuous (‖ω_j‖ → 0 when ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k), i.e. a current, with M(F_#X) ≤ Λ^k M(X).
 (b) ∂F_#X = F_#∂X (A1 for F_σ; ∂X ∈ NC_{k−1} since ∂∂X = 0).
 (c) If F is C^∞ (and Lipschitz), F_#X agrees with A1: DF_σ → DF and F_σ → F uniformly on spt X, so by the representation in A1, (F_σ)_#X(ω) → F_#X(ω) (A1 sense). In particular id_#X(ω) = X(ζω) = X(ω) by (VO).
 (d) spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X): if tsupport ω ∩ F(spt X) = ∅ then, by compactness, tsupport ω ∩ F_σ(spt X) = ∅ for small σ, so (F_σ)_#X(ω) = 0 (A1).
 (e) If F, G are Lipschitz with constants ≤ Λ and |F − G| ≤ δ on spt X, then |F_#X(ω) − G_#X(ω)| ≤ δ((2Λ)^k M(X)‖dω‖ + (2Λ)^{k−1}M(∂X)‖ω‖). (Apply A3 to F_σ, G_σ with sup_{spt X}|F_σ − G_σ| → sup_{spt X}|F − G|, then let σ ↓ 0.) In particular F_#X depends only on F|spt X. It is linear in X: F_#(X − Y) = F_#X − F_#Y for X, Y ∈ NC_k (true for each F_σ with a common cut-off ζ).
 (f) Homotopy formula. Let F, G be Λ-Lipschitz, X ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N), and let Ĥ : ℝ × ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be any Lipschitz map with Ĥ(t,x) = F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) on [0,1] × spt X. Then
 G_#X − F_#X = ∂Ĥ_#([[0,1]] × X) + Ĥ_#([[0,1]] × ∂X) (last term absent for k = 0), and
 M(Ĥ_#([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ sup_{spt X}|G − F|·(2Λ)^k M(X).
 Proof. By (e) in ℝ^{N+1} (applied to the currents [[0,1]] × X and [[0,1]] × ∂X of NC, whose supports lie in [0,1] × spt X), the right sides do not depend on the choice of Ĥ. Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^N), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of spt X, and let s be the function fixed above (s, s' bounded, s(t) = t on [−1, 2]). H_σ(t,x) := F_σ(x) + s(t)χ(x)(G_σ − F_σ)(x) is C^∞ and globally Lipschitz with a constant independent of σ ≤ 1. Indeed ∂_tH_σ = s'(t)χ(G_σ − F_σ) and D_xH_σ = DF_σ + s(t)(Dχ ⊗ (G_σ − F_σ) + χ(DG_σ − DF_σ)) are bounded, because s, s', χ, Dχ are bounded and G_σ − F_σ is bounded on the compact spt χ uniformly in σ ≤ 1. H_σ equals F_σ + t(G_σ − F_σ) near [0,1] × spt X, and converges uniformly to H := F + s(t)χ(G − F), which is Lipschitz and agrees with F + t(G − F) on [0,1] × spt X. By A3 for F_σ, G_σ:
 (G_σ)_#X − (F_σ)_#X = ∂H_{σ#}([[0,1]] × X) + H_{σ#}([[0,1]] × ∂X), M(H_{σ#}([[0,1]] × X)) ≤ sup_{spt X}|G_σ − F_σ|(2Λ)^k M(X).
 As σ ↓ 0, the left side converges weakly to G_#X − F_#X (definition). By (c), (e) in ℝ^{N+1}, H_{σ#}Y → H_#Y weakly for Y = [[0,1]] × X, [[0,1]] × ∂X. Boundaries converge weakly (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary), and lower semicontinuity of mass (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) gives the estimate with sup_{spt X}|G − F|.

Part B. Integrality (Simon 3.3–3.9 and 3.2(2)). Throughout, X = τ(M, θ, ξ) is integer multiplicity in 𝒟_k(ℝ^N), k ≥ 1, X ∈ NC_k. Replacing M by M ∩ spt X (IMC(b); by (MR) and (VO) the carrier part outside spt X is μ-null), we may assume M ⊆ spt X, so Hᵏ(M) ≤ ∫_M θ dHᵏ = M(X) < ∞ (MR). Hᵏ := μHE[k], and Lᵏ is Lebesgue measure.
7. B1 (Parametrization). There are countably many compact A_i ⊆ ℝᵏ, Lipschitz G_i : ℝᵏ → ℝ^N and κ_i > 0 such that: G_i is differentiable at every u ∈ A_i with DG_i(u) injective; |G_i(u) − G_i(v)| ≥ κ_i|u − v| on A_i; the sets G_i(A_i) ⊆ M are pairwise disjoint; and Hᵏ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0.
 Proof: by SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable, M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝᵏ), Hᵏ(M₀) = 0, F_j Lipschitz. By Rademacher (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), the differentiability set D_j of F_j is Borel with null complement, and Hᵏ(F_j(ℝᵏ ∖ D_j)) = 0 (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le). On Z_j := {u ∈ D_j : DF_j(u) not injective} the Jacobian vanishes, so Hᵏ(F_j(Z_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero). Let E_j := (D_j ∖ Z_j) ∩ F_j^{-1}(M). For injective A choose K_A > 0 with |Au| ≥ |u|/K_A (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith) and r(A) := 1/(2K_A) (r(A) := 1 otherwise). Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt covers E_j by disjoint Borel sets E_j ∩ t_l on which F_j approximates A_l = DF_j(y_l) with constant r(A_l); there |F_j(u) − F_j(v)| ≥ (2K_{A_l})^{-1}|u − v|. Enumerate the pieces and make the images disjoint inductively, E'_i := E_i ∖ G_i^{-1}(⋃_{i'<i}G_{i'}(E'_{i'})), which is Borel by Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn. By inner regularity, write each E'_i, up to an Lᵏ-null set (with Hᵏ-null image), as a countable disjoint union of compact sets.
8. B2 (Tangent planes of pieces). Let A ⊆ ℝᵏ be compact and G Lipschitz with |G(u) − G(v)| ≥ κ|u − v| on A and G differentiable on A. Then for Lᵏ-a.e. u ∈ A, V := DG(u)(ℝᵏ) is k-dimensional and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (G(A)) (G(u)) V.
 Proof: let u be a Lebesgue density point of A and a Lebesgue point of 1_A·JG. Density gives points v ∈ A with v − u = rw/|w| + o(r), so |DG(u)w| ≥ κ|w| and JG(u) > 0. Let x := G(u) and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). The injective area formula (SimonGMT injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn, weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum) and the scaling of Hᵏ give ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' G(A)} f dHᵏ = ∫_{ℝᵏ} 1_A(u + rw) f((G(u + rw) − G(u))/r) JG(u + rw) dw. The integrand vanishes for |w| ≥ ρ/κ. On B_{ρ/κ}, (G(u + rw) − G(u))/r → DG(u)w uniformly and 1_A(u + r·)JG(u + r·) → JG(u) in L¹. So the integral tends to ∫ f(DG(u)w)JG(u) dw = ∫_V f dHᵏ.
 Consequence: by B1 and (IMC)(a) (Hᵏ(M) < ∞), for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ G_i(A_i), T_xM exists and equals DG_i(u)(ℝᵏ), u = G_i^{-1}(x). By the orientation field and (L3), for a.e. u ∈ A_i,
 (B2′) ξ(G_i(u)) = s_i(u)Λ_kDG_i(u)(e)/JG_i(u), e := e_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ e_k, s_i(u) ∈ {1, −1} Borel.
9. B3 (The integral current is integer multiplicity). Let F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be Lipschitz. H_i := F ∘ G_i is Lipschitz. For a.e. u ∈ A_i put d^MF(G_iu) := DH_i(u)∘DG_i(u)^{-1} on T_{G_iu}M. Then ‖d^MF‖ ≤ Lip F, because |DH_i(u)w| = lim_{t↓0}|F(G_i(u + tw)) − F(G_i(u))|/t ≤ Lip F·|DG_i(u)w|. So J^MF := |Λ_k(d^MF)ξ| ≤ Lip(F)^k by (L1), and I_F := ∫_M J^MFθ dHᵏ ≤ Lip(F)^k M(X). Define
 Φ_F(ω) := ∫_M θ⟨ω(F(x)), Λ_k(d^MF(x))ξ(x)⟩ dHᵏ.
 By the area formula for G_i on A_i, (B2′) and Λ_k(d^MF)Λ_kDG_i(e) = Λ_kDH_i(e):
 Φ_F(ω) = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i s_i⟨ω(H_i(u)), Λ_kDH_i(u)(e)⟩ du, Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i JH_i du ≤ I_F (θ_i := θ∘G_i),
 absolutely convergent. Where DH_i(u) is not injective, Λ_kDH_i(u)(e) = 0. Partition A_i^+ := {u ∈ A_i : H_i differentiable at u, DH_i(u) injective} as in B1 into compact pieces A_{il} (up to an Lᵏ-null set) on which H_i is injective with |H_i(u) − H_i(v)| ≥ κ_{il}|u − v|. Put N_{il} := H_i(A_{il}) (compact), g_{il} := (θ_is_i)∘(H_i|A_{il})^{-1} ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, and η_{il} := (Λ_kDH_i(e)/JH_i)∘(H_i|A_{il})^{-1} (a unit simple k-vector by (L3)). The injective area formula for H_i on A_{il} gives
 Φ_F(ω) = Σ_{i,l} Φ_{il}(ω), Φ_{il}(ω) := ∫_{N_{il}} g_{il}⟨ω, η_{il}⟩ dHᵏ, Σ_{i,l} ∫_{N_{il}} |g_{il}| dHᵏ ≤ I_F < ∞.
 Each Φ_{il} is an integer multiplicity current, since (N_{il}, |g_{il}|, sign(g_{il})η_{il}) is an IMRep:
 - N_{il} is compact and countably k-rectifiable (a Lipschitz image of A_{il}, extended to ℝᵏ by Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi), with Hᵏ(N_{il}) ≤ ∫|g_{il}| < ∞;
 - the multiplicity is a positive integer and the orientation is Borel;
 - by B2 applied to H_i on A_{il}, the approximate tangent space of N_{il} at Hᵏ-a.e. point H_i(u) is DH_i(u)(ℝᵏ), which η_{il} orients.
 Each Φ_{il} is a current (linear, and |Φ_{il}(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖∫|g_{il}| dHᵏ gives sequential continuity; it is the action of the IMRep just described) with M(Φ_{il}) ≤ ∫|g_{il}| dHᵏ, so Σ_{il}M(Φ_{il}) < ∞. Enumerate the countably many pairs (i, l) by ℕ, padding with zero currents. IMS (degree k = (k − 1) + 1) gives an integer multiplicity current S with S(ω) = Σ_{il}Φ_{il}(ω) = Φ_F(ω) for every ω. Hence Φ_F is (the action of) an integer multiplicity current.
10. B4 (Identification). F_#X (A4) = Φ_F.
 Lemma (weak continuity of pull-backs). Let H_σ, H : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{N'} be Lipschitz near a compact A with sup_σ Lip H_σ < ∞ and H_σ → H uniformly near A. Then for ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(ℝ^{N'}) and w ∈ L¹(A), ∫_A w(H_σ^#ω)(e) du → ∫_A w(H^#ω)(e) du.
 Proof: (H^#ω)(e) = Σ_J ω_J(H) det D(H^{j_1},…,H^{j_k}) is uniformly bounded, so by density we may take w ∈ C_c^∞. Since ω_J(H_σ) → ω_J(H) uniformly, it suffices to show ∫ c det Dv_σ → ∫ c det Dv for continuous compactly supported c and Lipschitz v_σ → v uniformly with bounded constants. Prove by induction on r ≤ k that ∫ β ∧ dv_σ^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv_σ^r → ∫ β ∧ dv^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^r for every continuous compactly supported (k − r)-form β. For smooth β, integrate by parts: ∫ β ∧ dv_σ^1 ∧ R_σ = ±∫ v_σ^1 dβ ∧ R_σ. This is valid for Lipschitz functions by mollification: the a.e. derivative of a Lipschitz function is its weak derivative (Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq), and D(v ∗ φ_δ) = (Dv) ∗ φ_δ → Dv a.e. and boundedly (Mathlib ContDiffBump.ae_convolution_tendsto_right_of_locallyIntegrable). Then ∫ v_σ^1 dβ ∧ R_σ − ∫ v^1 dβ ∧ R = ∫(v_σ^1 − v^1)dβ ∧ R_σ + ∫ v^1 dβ ∧ (R_σ − R) → 0, by uniform convergence and the induction hypothesis for the continuous form v^1dβ. General continuous β follow by uniform approximation and the uniform bounds.
 Now (F_σ)_#X(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(F_σ(x)), Λ_kDF_σ(x)ξ(x)⟩ dHᵏ (A1) = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_is_i(H_{i,σ}^#ω)(e) du with H_{i,σ} := F_σ∘G_i (area formula, (B2′), chain rule). Each term converges to ∫_{A_i} θ_is_i(H_i^#ω)(e) du by the lemma (w = θ_is_i1_{A_i} ∈ L¹ since JG_i ≥ κ_i^k on A_i). The i-th term is bounded by ‖ω‖Lip(F)^k∫_{G_i(A_i)}θ dHᵏ, which is summable. By dominated convergence for series the limit is Σ_i ∫_{A_i}θ_is_i(H_i^#ω)(e) du = Φ_F(ω) (computation in B3). Hence F_#X = Φ_F is integer multiplicity.
11. B5 (Products). [[0,1]] × X = τ((0,1) × M, θ∘pr, e₀ ∧ ξ) is integer multiplicity in ℝ^{N+1} (coordinates (t, x) as in A2).
 Product-null lemma: if Hᵏ(Z) = 0 then H^{k+1}(I × Z) = 0 for every bounded interval I. Cover Z by sets C_j with 0 < d_j := max(diam C_j, ε 2^{−j}) < 1 and Σ d_j^k < 2ε (enlarging degenerate sets), and cover I × C_j by ⌈|I|/d_j⌉ sets of diameter ≤ √2 d_j; the sum of (diameter)^{k+1} is ≤ c(|I| + 1)Σ_j d_j^k.
 The maps Ĝ_i(t,u) := (t, G_i(u)) on [0,1] × A_i are injective, bi-Lipschitz (constant min(1, κ_i)) and differentiable with JĜ_i(t,u) = JG_i(u). By the area formula, H^{k+1}⌞((0,1) × G_i(A_i)) is the product of L¹⌞(0,1) and Hᵏ⌞G_i(A_i). By B2, the approximate tangent space of [0,1] × G_i(A_i) at a.e. point is ℝe₀ ⊕ DG_i(u)(ℝᵏ); with (IMC)(a), the same holds for (0,1) × M, oriented by the unit simple (k+1)-vector e₀ ∧ ξ. Fubini and A2 give ∫_{(0,1)×M} θ⟨ω, e₀ ∧ ξ⟩ dH^{k+1} = ∫_0^1∫_M θ⟨ω₁(t,·), ξ⟩ dHᵏ dt = ([[0,1]] × X)(ω). The remaining IMRep fields are immediate.
12. B6 (Summary). If Y ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N) is integer multiplicity (k ≥ 1) and F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}, Ĥ : ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ^{N'} are Lipschitz, then F_#Y and Ĥ_#([[0,1]] × Y) are integer multiplicity (B3, B4, and B5 with A2 for the normality of [[0,1]] × Y).

Part C. The operators (N = N' = P).
13. C1 (Definitions). For k ∈ ℕ, F, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P):
 push k F X := F_#X (A4) if F is Lipschitz and X ∈ NC_k, and 0 otherwise;
 homot k F G X := Ĥ_X#([[0,1]] × X) if F, G are Lipschitz, X ∈ NC_k and spt X ≠ ∅, and 0 otherwise, where Ĥ_X(t,x) := F(x) + c(t)χ_X(x)(G(x) − F(x)), c(t) := min(1, max(0, t)), χ_X(x) := max(0, 1 − dist(x, spt X)).
 For spt X ≠ ∅, Ĥ_X is Lipschitz on ℝ × ℝ^P: χ_X is 1-Lipschitz, bounded, and vanishes outside the compact set {dist(·, spt X) ≤ 1}, on which G − F is bounded and Lipschitz; c is 1-Lipschitz and bounded. Also Ĥ_X(t,x) = F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) on [0,1] × spt X. By A4(e) in ℝ^{P+1} (supports of [[0,1]] × X in [0,1] × spt X), homot k F G X = Ĥ_#([[0,1]] × X) for every Lipschitz Ĥ with this property (C1′). (C1′) also holds when spt X = ∅: then X = 0 by (VO), so both sides are 0.
Fix Λ and Λ-Lipschitz F, G, F', G'; let X, Y ∈ NC_k(ℝ^P).
14. C2 (Identity). push k id X = X by A4(c).
15. C3 (Linearity). push k F (X − Y) = push k F X − push k F Y by A4(e) (X − Y ∈ NC_k). For homot, let χ be a Lipschitz cut-off with compact support equal to 1 on spt X ∪ spt Y ⊇ spt(X − Y), and Ĥ := F + c(t)χ(G − F). By (C1′) all three homotopy currents are Ĥ_# of [[0,1]] × X, [[0,1]] × Y, [[0,1]] × (X − Y), and both [[0,1]] × · and Ĥ_# are linear (A2, A4(e) in ℝ^{P+1}).
16. C4 (Locality). If F = F' and G = G' on spt X, then push k F X = push k F' X by A4(e) (δ = 0). Ĥ_X (built from F, G) equals F' + t(G' − F') on [0,1] × spt X, so homot k F G X = homot k F' G' X by (C1′).
17. C5 (Mass and support). M(push k F X) ≤ Λ^k M(X) and spt push k F X ⊆ F(spt X) by A4(a), (d). If dist(F(x), G(x)) ≤ δ on spt X, then M(homot k F G X) ≤ δ(2Λ)^k M(X) by A4(f) applied with Ĥ_X (if spt X = ∅ then X = 0 by (VO) and both sides vanish, so negative δ is harmless). spt homot k F G X ⊆ Ĥ_X(spt([[0,1]] × X)) ⊆ Ĥ_X([0,1] × spt X) = {F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) : x ∈ spt X, t ∈ [0,1]} by A4(d) in ℝ^{P+1}.
18. C6 (Degree k + 1: boundary, homotopy formula, integrality). Let X ∈ NC_{k+1}(ℝ^P). (∂ push (k+1) F X) = push k F ∂X by A4(b) (∂X ∈ NC_k). Apply A4(f) with Ĥ := Ĥ_X, which agrees with F + t(G − F) on [0,1] × spt ∂X as well, so by (C1′) Ĥ_X#([[0,1]] × ∂X) = homot k F G ∂X. This gives push (k+1) G X − push (k+1) F X = ∂ homot (k+1) F G X + homot k F G ∂X, i.e. push (k+1) G X − push (k+1) F X − homot k F G ∂X = ∂(homot (k+1) F G X) (GeometricCurrentOn.ext; the contract's subtraction is pointwise). If X is integer multiplicity, push (k+1) F X and homot (k+1) F G X are integer multiplicity by B6.
19. C7 (Degree 0). For X ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^P) with compact support and finite mass (∂ is not defined in degree 0 and boundaryMassOn X univ = 0), A4(f) with k = 0 gives push 0 G X − push 0 F X = ∂ homot 0 F G X.
20. C8. The pair (push, homot) of C1 satisfies the six conjuncts of the statement by C2, C3, C4, C5, C6 and C7. ∎
proof_key_steps: Representation of finite-mass currents with compact support (REP, VO) and multilinear estimates (L0)–(L3).
Smooth push-forward with cut-off, its boundary, support and mass bound; product [[0,1]] × X with ∂([[0,1]] × X) = {1} × X − {0} × X − [[0,1]] × ∂X; smooth homotopy formula with mass estimate.

Lipschitz push-forward as the limit of mollified push-forwards, with mass and support bounds, boundary commutation, locality/linearity estimate (e), and the homotopy formula for Lipschitz maps via cut-off homotopies and lower semicontinuity of mass.

Integrality: Lipschitz parametrization of the carrier, approximate tangent planes of pieces via the area formula, integer pieces of Φ_F summed by IMS, identification F_#X = Φ_F by weak continuity of Jacobian minors, and integrality of [[0,1]] × X.

Operators: push := F_#X, homot := Ĥ_X#([[0,1]] × X) with a cut-off straight-line homotopy (0 when spt X = ∅); verification of identity, linearity, locality, mass/support bounds, homotopy formula and integrality.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (1)–(25) (chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1928), as written out in steps E1–E5 of the parent proof. Differences from the parent's text:
 - the good centre, the retraction, the push-forward/homotopy calculus and the summation of integer multiplicity pieces are the sibling theorems cmcdt_good_center (GC), cmcdt_skeleton_retraction (RET), cmcdt_lipschitz_pushforward_homotopy (PF) and cmcdt_im_series (IMS);
 - the parent's X_ν are decomposed into the dyadic shells already used in its E3, and each shell is deformed with its own Lipschitz extension of ψ;
 - integrality of Q₀ and R₁ is obtained by summing the integer multiplicity shell contributions with IMS (this is the closing step of the parent's B3, applied directly to ψ_#X_0 + Σ_i ψ_#Y_i = Q₀ as in the parent's E4).

Notation. n := m + 1. (VO), (MR), (REP), (IMC), (SL) are the five displayed hypotheses (frozen types of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds). All currents are on univ in ℝ^P. For currents A, B, “A + B” abbreviates A − (0 − B) (the contract's subtraction is pointwise, and currents are equal when their values agree, GeometricCurrentOn.ext). ‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)|, and |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖ for every current X. NC_k := k-currents with compact support, finite mass and (k ≥ 1) finite boundary mass; NC_k is closed under differences. Support facts used below (all from the definitions and (VO)): spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B; spt ∂A ⊆ spt A; spt 0 = ∅; a current that vanishes on every test form whose support is disjoint from a closed set E has support in E (every x ∉ E has a ball with compact closure disjoint from E). L_n := {x : ∃ s, P ≤ n + |s|, x_i ∈ ℤ (i ∈ s)} is closed (a finite union of the closed sets {x : x_i ∈ ℤ, i ∈ s}).

1. Trivial cases. If n ≥ P then L_n = ℝ^P (s = ∅). Take Q₀ := T, R₁ := 0, S₁ := 0 and c := 1: T − T − 0 = 0 = ∂0, T and 0 are integer multiplicity, the mass bounds are equalities or 0 ≤ ·, and spt T ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt T), spt ∂T ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T), spt 0 = ∅. From now on n < P, so RET and GC apply. Let c_R > 0 be RET's constant, C_G := (GC's constant) + 1 > 0, c₄ := 8(1 + √P c_R), and
 c := max(1, c₄ⁿ(1 + 2C_G), √P 2ⁿ c₄ⁿ(1 + 2C_G), √P (2c₄)^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G), c₄^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)),
 which depends only on P and m. Let (push, homot) be the operators given by PF applied to (VO), (MR), (REP), (IMC). The zero current (in every degree) is integer multiplicity: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it (∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable, the remaining fields hold vacuously, and the representing integral over ∅ is 0). Let T be as in the statement. If M(T) = 0 then T = 0 (|T(ω)| ≤ M(T)‖ω‖), ∂T = 0, and Q₀ = R₁ = S₁ = 0 work. Assume M(T) > 0.

2. Measures (parent E0, E2). Let R_T = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of T and μ_T := R_T.measure. By (MR), μ_T(W) = M_W(T) for open W, so μ_T(ℝ^P) = M(T) < ∞, and μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ spt T) = 0 by (VO). Further:
 - T(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ_T (definition of Represents and of the density measure);
 - ξ is μ_T-a.e. strongly measurable (μ_T ≪ Hⁿ⌞M);
 - |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ_T-a.e. by (IMC)(d);
 - μ_T is finite on compact sets.
 Since M(∂T) < ∞, (REP) (U = univ) gives μ_∂, ξ_∂ with μ_∂(W) = M_W(∂T) for open W, |ξ_∂| ≤ 1 and ∂T(η) = ∫ ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂; moreover μ_∂(ℝ^P) = M(∂T) and μ_∂(ℝ^P ∖ spt ∂T) = 0 by (VO).

3. Good centre (parent E1; GC). GC applied to the finite measures μ_T, μ_∂ gives a with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 such that, for d := dist(·, L*(a)), L*(a) the set of y with at least m + 2 coordinates in a_i + ℤ,
 (6) μ_T({d < r}) ≤ C_G r^{n+1} M(T), (7) μ_∂({d < r}) ≤ C_G r^{n+1} M(∂T) for r ∈ (0, 1/4].
 In particular μ_T({d = 0}) = μ_∂({d = 0}) = 0.

4. Retraction (RET). RET with this a gives ψ with: if d(x) > 0 then ψ(x) ∈ L_n and |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P; and ψ is (c_R/r)-Lipschitz on {d ≥ r} for r ∈ (0, 1/4]. For r ∈ (0, 1/4] let φ_r be the componentwise McShane extension of ψ|{d ≥ r} (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real for each coordinate x ↦ ψ(x)_i, which is (c_R/r)-Lipschitz on {d ≥ r}). Then φ_r : ℝ^P → ℝ^P is (√P c_R/r)-Lipschitz and φ_r = ψ on {d ≥ r}. Put Λ(r) := max(1, √P c_R/r); id and φ_r are Λ(r)-Lipschitz, and Λ(r) ≤ c₄2^j whenever r ≥ 2^{−j−3}.

5. Slicing and good radii (parent E2; Simon (8)–(10)). Apply (SL) with U = univ, k = m, T, μ := μ_T, μ' := μ_∂, ξ, ξ' := ξ_∂, f := d, L := 1 (d is 1-Lipschitz; the measures are finite on compact sets, and the a.e. bounds and representations hold by 2). This gives currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_n, B_t ∈ 𝒟_{n−1} with A_t(ω) = ∫_{d<t} ξ(ω) dμ_T, B_t(η) = ∫_{d<t} ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂, ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) when tsupport η ∩ {d = t} = ∅, and, for Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t, M(Z_t) ≤ liminf_{h↓0} h^{−1}μ_T({t − h < d < t}). If m ≥ 1, write m = k' + 1 and apply (SL) also to ∂T, which has degree k' + 1 (k := k' = m − 1, μ := μ_∂, ξ := ξ_∂, μ' := 0, ξ' := 0, valid because ∂∂T = 0; f := d). Its A'_t has the same values as B_t, so A'_t = B_t; its B'_t = 0; and M(∂B_t) ≤ liminf_{h↓0} h^{−1}μ_∂({t − h < d < t}).
 F(t) := μ_T({d < t}) and F_∂(t) := μ_∂({d < t}) are nondecreasing and finite, and μ_T({t − h < d < t}) ≤ F(t) − F(t − h), likewise for μ_∂. At every t where F and F_∂ are differentiable (all t outside a Lebesgue null set, Mathlib Monotone.ae_differentiableAt), M(Z_t) ≤ F'(t) and M(∂B_t) ≤ F_∂'(t) < ∞. For ν ≥ 0 let ρ_ν := 2^{−ν−2}. F' is measurable and ∫_{ρ_ν/2}^{ρ_ν} F' ≤ F(ρ_ν) − F(ρ_ν/2) ≤ μ_T({d < ρ_ν}) ≤ C_G ρ_ν^{n+1}M(T) (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv, MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc, and (6)). By Markov's inequality, F' > 4C_Gρ_νⁿM(T) on a subset of (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) of measure ≤ ρ_ν/4. As (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) has length ρ_ν/2 > ρ_ν/4, there is r_ν := ρ*_ν ∈ (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) at which F and F_∂ are differentiable and F'(r_ν) ≤ 4C_Gρ_νⁿM(T). Hence
 (10) M(Z_{r_ν}) ≤ 4C_Gρ_νⁿM(T) and M(∂B_{r_ν}) < ∞ (if m ≥ 1).
 (The parent also asks μ_T({d = r_ν}) = 0; this is not needed below because the shells are taken half-open.)
 Since r_{ν+1} < ρ_{ν+1} = ρ_ν/2 < r_ν, the r_ν strictly decrease to 0, r_ν ≤ 1/4 and r_ν > 2^{−ν−3}. Write A_ν := A_{r_ν}, B_ν := B_{r_ν}, Z_ν := Z_{r_ν}.

6. The pieces (parent E3). For j ≥ 0 define W_0 := T − A_0, W_j := A_{j−1} − A_j (j ≥ 1), D_0 := ∂T − B_0, D_j := B_{j−1} − B_j (j ≥ 1). Let E_0 := {d ≥ r_0} and E_j := {r_j ≤ d < r_{j−1}} (j ≥ 1).
 (6a) W_j(ω) = ∫_{E_j} ξ(ω) dμ_T and D_j(η) = ∫_{E_j} ξ_∂(η) dμ_∂. Hence M(W_0) ≤ M(T) and M(D_0) ≤ M(∂T), and for j ≥ 1, by (6), (7) with r_{j−1} < ρ_{j−1} = 2^{−j−1}: M(W_j) ≤ C_G 2^{−(j+1)(n+1)}M(T) and M(D_j) ≤ C_G 2^{−(j+1)(n+1)}M(∂T).
 (6b) W_j is integer multiplicity: (IMC)(b) with E := E_j gives a current represented by (M ∩ E_j, θ, ξ), whose values are ∫_{E_j} ξ(ω) dμ_T = W_j(ω).
 (6c) Supports: spt W_j ⊆ spt T ∩ closure(E_j) ⊆ spt T ∩ {d ≥ r_j} and spt D_j ⊆ spt ∂T ∩ {d ≥ r_j}. Indeed, if ω vanishes on spt T ∩ closure(E_j), the integrand of (6a) vanishes μ_T-a.e. on E_j (μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ spt T) = 0), so W_j vanishes on forms supported off this closed set. spt Z_j ⊆ {d = r_j} by the third clause of (SL). Also spt A_t ⊆ spt T and spt B_t ⊆ spt ∂T ⊆ spt T, so all supports above are compact.
 (6d) Boundaries: ∂A_t = B_t + Z_t, hence ∂W_0 = D_0 − Z_0 and ∂W_j = D_j + Z_{j−1} − Z_j (j ≥ 1). For m ≥ 1, ∂D_0 = −∂B_0, ∂D_j = ∂B_{j−1} − ∂B_j and ∂Z_j = −∂B_j have finite mass by (10). Hence W_j ∈ NC_n and D_j, Z_j ∈ NC_{n−1} (for m = 0 there is no boundary condition in degree 0).
 (6e) Σ_{j=0}^{N} W_j = T − A_N and M(A_N) ≤ μ_T({d < r_N}) ≤ C_G ρ_N^{n+1}M(T) → 0.

7. Deforming the pieces (parent E3, (11)–(20)). For j ≥ 0 let φ_j := φ_{r_j} and Λ_j := Λ(r_j) ≤ c₄2^j (as r_j > 2^{−j−3}); Λ_j ≤ Λ_{j+1}. Then φ_j = ψ on spt W_j ∪ spt D_j ∪ spt Z_j ⊆ {d ≥ r_j}, and φ_{j+1} = ψ = φ_j on spt Z_j ⊆ {d = r_j} ⊆ {d ≥ r_{j+1}}. Define
 V_j := push n φ_j W_j, H_j := homot n id φ_j W_j, Y_j := push (n−1) φ_j D_j, E'_j := homot (n−1) id φ_j D_j, L_j := push (n−1) φ_j Z_j, K_j := homot (n−1) id φ_j Z_j.
 - By PF (locality, maps Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz): push (n−1) φ_{j+1} Z_j = L_j and homot (n−1) id φ_{j+1} Z_j = K_j.
 - By PF (identity and homotopy formula in degree n = m + 1, with F = id, G = φ_j, Λ = Λ_j): V_j − W_j − homot (n−1) id φ_j (∂W_j) = ∂H_j.
 - By PF (linearity, all pieces in NC_{n−1}) and (6d): homot (n−1) id φ_j (∂W_0) = E'_0 − K_0 and homot (n−1) id φ_j (∂W_j) = E'_j + K_{j−1} − K_j (j ≥ 1).
 - By PF (boundary commutation and linearity): ∂V_0 = Y_0 − L_0 and ∂V_j = Y_j + L_{j−1} − L_j (j ≥ 1).
 Summing over j = 0,…,N (telescoping):
 (S1) Σ_{j≤N}(V_j − W_j − ∂H_j) = Σ_{j≤N}E'_j − K_N, (S2) ∂(Σ_{j≤N}V_j) = Σ_{j≤N}Y_j − L_N.
 W_j is integer multiplicity, so by the integrality clause of PF (degree k + 1 = n), push n φ_j W_j = V_j is integer multiplicity (with F := φ_j) and homot n id φ_j W_j = H_j is integer multiplicity (with F := id, G := φ_j).
 Estimates (PF mass bounds; |φ_j(x) − x| = |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √P on the supports, since d > 0 there):
 M(V_0) ≤ c₄ⁿM(T), M(V_j) ≤ c₄ⁿ2^{jn}C_G2^{−(j+1)(n+1)}M(T) ≤ c₄ⁿC_G2^{−j}M(T);
 M(H_0) ≤ √P(2c₄)ⁿM(T), M(H_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)ⁿC_G2^{−j}M(T);
 M(Y_0) ≤ c₄^{n−1}M(∂T), M(Y_j) ≤ c₄^{n−1}C_G2^{−2j}M(∂T); M(E'_0) ≤ √P(2c₄)^{n−1}M(∂T), M(E'_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)^{n−1}C_G2^{−2j}M(∂T);
 M(L_N) ≤ Λ_{N}^{n−1}M(Z_N) ≤ c₄^{n−1}2^{N(n−1)}·4C_G2^{−(N+2)n}M(T) ≤ 4C_Gc₄^{n−1}2^{−N}M(T) → 0, and likewise M(K_N) ≤ √P(2Λ_N)^{n−1}M(Z_N) → 0.
 Hence Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ c₄ⁿ(1 + 2C_G)M(T), Σ_j M(H_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)ⁿ(1 + 2C_G)M(T), Σ_j M(E'_j) ≤ √P(2c₄)^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)M(∂T) and Σ_j M(Y_j) ≤ c₄^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)M(∂T).

8. Limits (parent E4; IMS).
 - IMS (degree n = m + 1) gives Q₀ with Q₀(ω) = Σ_j V_j(ω): integer multiplicity, M(Q₀) ≤ Σ_j M(V_j) ≤ cM(T), spt Q₀ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt V_j.
 - By (IMC)(c), 0 − H_j is integer multiplicity (0 and H_j are), with M(0 − H_j) ≤ M(H_j). IMS (degree m + 2) gives R₁ with R₁(ζ) = Σ_j(0 − H_j)(ζ): integer multiplicity, M(R₁) ≤ cM(T), spt R₁ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt H_j.
 - IMS (degree m + 1, existence part) gives S₁ with S₁(ω) = Σ_j(0 − E'_j)(ω), M(S₁) ≤ cM(∂T), spt S₁ ⊆ closure ⋃_j spt E'_j.
 Identity (21). Evaluate (S1) at ω: Σ_{j≤N}V_j(ω) − T(ω) + A_N(ω) − Σ_{j≤N}H_j(dω) = Σ_{j≤N}E'_j(ω) − K_N(ω). As N → ∞, A_N(ω) → 0 and K_N(ω) → 0 (masses → 0), so Q₀(ω) − T(ω) + R₁(dω) = −S₁(ω), i.e. (T − Q₀ − S₁)(ω) = ∂R₁(ω). Hence T − Q₀ − S₁ = R₁.boundary.
 Boundary mass (25). The finite sums Ŝ_N := Σ_{j≤N}V_j converge weakly to Q₀, so ∂Ŝ_N converge weakly to ∂Q₀ (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary), and M(∂Q₀) ≤ liminf_N M(∂Ŝ_N) (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf). By (S2), M(∂Ŝ_N) ≤ Σ_jM(Y_j) + M(L_N), so M(∂Q₀) ≤ c₄^{n−1}(1 + 2C_G)M(∂T) ≤ cM(∂T).

9. Supports (parent E5, (22)–(23)).
 - spt V_j ⊆ φ_j(spt W_j) = ψ(spt W_j) ⊆ L_n ∩ cthickening(√P, spt T) (RET, as d > 0 and the points lie in spt T). Both sets are closed, so spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n ∩ cthickening(√P, spt T).
 - spt H_j ⊆ {x + t(φ_j(x) − x) : x ∈ spt W_j, t ∈ [0,1]} ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt T) (PF), so spt R₁ ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt T) (spt(0 − H_j) ⊆ spt H_j).
 - Likewise spt E'_j ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T), so spt S₁ ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T).
 - Finally, if tsupport ω ∩ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T) = ∅, then Y_j(ω) = 0 for all j (spt Y_j ⊆ φ_j(spt D_j) ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T); (VO)). So ∂Ŝ_N(ω) = −L_N(ω) → 0 and ∂Q₀(ω) = lim ∂Ŝ_N(ω) = 0; hence spt ∂Q₀ ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂T).

10. Q₀, R₁, S₁ satisfy all conclusions with the constant c of 1 (c ≥ 1): integrality (8), the identity (8), spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n (9), the four mass bounds (7)–(8) and the support inclusions (9). ∎
proof_key_steps: Trivial cases n ≥ P (Q₀ := T) and T = 0; constants from RET and GC.
Measures μ_T (IMRep, MR, VO) and μ_∂ (REP); good centre a with μ_T, μ_∂({d < r}) ≤ C r^{n+1}·mass (GC).
Retraction ψ (RET) and its McShane extensions φ_r with Lipschitz constant √P c_R/r.
Slicing (SL) and Lebesgue differentiation of F(t) = μ_T({d < t}) give radii r_ν ∈ (ρ_ν/2, ρ_ν) with M(Z_{r_ν}) ≤ 4Cρ_νⁿM(T) and finite boundary slices.
Dyadic shells W_j, D_j (integer multiplicity, normal, supports in {d ≥ r_j}) with ∂W_j = D_j + Z_{j−1} − Z_j.
PF: deformations V_j, homotopies H_j, E'_j; telescoping of the slice terms by locality; geometric mass estimates.
IMS: Q₀ := ΣV_j and R₁ := Σ(0 − H_j) integer multiplicity, S₁ := Σ(0 − E'_j); identity T − Q₀ − S₁ = ∂R₁; M(∂Q₀) by lower semicontinuity.
Supports: ψ maps into L_n and moves points by ≤ √P; homotopy supports; ∂Q₀ via vanishing of the deformed ∂T-pieces and of the slice terms in the limit.

subproblems.statement: Assume, as hypotheses of the statement, (VO) the frozen type of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support: for all P, n, U, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0; (MR) the frozen type of Submission.cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure: for U open and an IMRep R representing T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W; (IMC) the frozen type of Submission.cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces for Borel M ⊆ M' ⊆ U with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ (K ⊆ U compact); (b) the restriction (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) of an IMRep to a Borel E is an IMRep representing some current; (c) A − B is integer multiplicity for integer multiplicity A, B (U open); (d) |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for Hⁿ-a.e. x in the carrier. (These are exactly the frozen Lean types of the parent node's resolved dependencies, written as antecedents so that the child does not need those declarations; the parent instantiates them.) For all P, m ∈ ℕ (n := m + 1) there is c ∈ ℝ≥0 with c ≥ 1 such that for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P and every Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 there is a finite set 𝒬₀ of currents in 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (domain univ) with the following property: if Q₀ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, spt Q₀ ⊆ K, spt Q₀ ⊆ L_n := {x : there is a set s of coordinate indices with P ≤ n + |s| and x_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s}, M(Q₀) ≤ Λ and M(∂Q₀) < ∞, then there is Pc ∈ 𝒬₀ such that Pc and ∂Pc are integer multiplicity, Pc = 0 or M(Pc) ≥ 1, M(Pc) ≤ cM(Q₀), M(∂Pc) ≤ cM(∂Q₀), M(Q₀ − Pc) ≤ cM(∂Q₀), spt Pc ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt Q₀) and spt(Q₀ − Pc) ∪ spt ∂Pc ⊆ cthickening(√P, spt ∂Q₀).
